newsitem.title: UK: Ample supples keep sentiment weak for NWE gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Ample supples keep sentiment weak for NWE gas oil.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices and spot differentials weakened further on Wednesday, but despite the losses and a shallower IPE futures backwardation buyers were reluctant to be drawn out, traders said.
They said ample supply of Russian cargoes, lack of arbitrage opportunities and above normal temperatures in much of Europe were keeping spot market sentiment weak.

IPE gas oil dipped in early trade on U.S. stock data showing year-ago stock levels for U.S. distillates had moved into surplus for the first time since June 1995. The Feb contract ended $2 down at $201, the middle of a $5.50 trading range.

The Feb/March backwardation, the focus of attention for both spot and futures traders because of a perceived squeeze by one U.S. trade house, narrowed slightly to around $7.50 after stretching out to $10 on Tuesday.

Prompt heating oil barges traded at Feb IPE evens and Feb IPE -75 cents a tonne, fob ARA, for refinery and storage product respectively, but Feb 16-28 barrels were clinging onto a small premium, they said.
Russian cargoes were talked at Feb IPE -50/+25 cents cif NWE after trading down to +25 cents on Tuesday.
